title: enrich streamed responses with metadata propagation and per-endpoint telemetry
author: Aisha Patel
body: Motivation: Streaming endpoints and the OpenAI compatibility shim currently emit minimal telemetry which makes it hard to stitch tool/function-call execution, partial stream fragments, and final response metrics in a single trace. This PR adds hop-by-hop propagation of request metadata through stream fragments, attaches per-endpoint telemetry tags to emitted metrics, and ensures function/tool-call spans surface the original request id and route information. Design summary: 1) attach a compact request metadata header (X-RW-Req: req_id|route|stage) to streaming chunk handshake and to internal tool RPC calls, 2) enrich structured JSONL access logs with endpoint, model_variant, route_tag and request_latency_ms, 3) propagate trace-context (W3C traceparent) into internal tool runner and include span references in the stream fragment payload, 4) add a per-route metrics tag layer so metrics collection (latency/p50/p95, token_count) can be filtered by route and OpenAI-compat route alias. Backwards compatibility: header is optional; older clients continue to work. The OpenAI shim will synthesize the header when an incoming OpenAI-compatible request lacks one so downstream systems see consistent tags. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on a per-cluster basis behind ff.obs.stream-meta. Start with internal canary traffic for 48h, then enable for 25% production traffic for 72h, then full rollout. Migration notes: observability consumers should update parsers to read the new JSONL fields: route_tag, request_id, traceparent, tool_span_id. Implementation details: server/api/stream_handler.go: adds handshake negotiation to exchange X-RW-Req and populates stream fragment metadata. pkg/telemetry/headers.go: header encoder/decoder and validation. pkg/logging/jsonl_writer.go: new structured keys and rate-limited marshalling for high-frequency streaming events. agents/openai_shim/adapter.go: synthesize headers for legacy OpenAI-compatible requests and map openai.endpoint->route_tag. internal/toolrunner/client.go: propagate traceparent and attach parent_request_id to tool spans. Testing: unit tests for header encoding decode and property-based tests for corner-case separators. End-to-end e2e test exercises a multi-fragment streaming response that triggers a function call, asserts trace continuity and ensures final log emits request_latency_ms and tokens_emitted. Performance note: added micro-benchmark; minimal median latency impact (~0.3ms) and small memory for header allocations. Checklist: [x] header encoder/decoder implemented [x] stream handshake updated [x] toolrunner propagation added [x] jsonl fields added and backward safe [x] tests and e2e added [x] docs updated. Related: addresses ENG-1874 (trace fragmentation debugging) and ENG-1902 (openai shim telemetry gaps).
commits_summary: feat(obs): stream handshake metadata and header codec
feat(openai-shim): synthesize request metadata when missing
chore(tests): add e2e coverage for cross-span streaming flow
review_thread: Marco: Overall looks good, one question on header size and separator collision—can you confirm the encoding handles edge chars?
Aisha: Yes, header uses base64 URL-safe encoding for any payload with predictable separator-free output. Added unit tests for separators.
Lena: Left comment to add a minor lint fix in jsonl_writer.go to reduce allocation; also suggested adding a metrics tag for model_variant.
Aisha: Addressed both comments; added model_variant to emitted tags and refactored marshalling to reduce alloc.
Olivia: Approved after CI green and a successful e2e run on staging.
ci_checks: e2e-streaming: pass (flaky on first run, rerun fixed)
release_notes: Observability: streaming endpoints now emit request_id, route_tag, and traceparent in structured logs
OpenAI shim: synthesizes request metadata headers for backward compatibility
Metrics: per-endpoint tags available for latency and token metrics enabling route-level dashboards
